metadata.title: Markets News: June 5, 2026: Nasdaq Ends Day 4% Lower, Tech Stocks Plunge; S&P 500 Snaps 9-Week Winning Streak; Treasury Yields Rise; Bitcoin Drops Below $60,000

content.text:
Tech stocks stocks plunged Friday, with the Nasdaq closing 4% lower, while Treasury yields surged after the monthly U.S. employment report indicated more jobs were added than expected in May and investors predicted higher interest rates for longer.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite, benchmark S&P 500, and blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average ended down a respective 4.2%, 2.6%, and 1.4%, with all three finishing lower for the week. The Nasdaq and S&P 500 recorded their worst weekly performances since April 2025 and May 2025, respectively.
The Nasdaq and Dow fell more than 1,100 and nearly 700 points today, respectively, while the S&P 500 snapped a nine-week losing streak.
Broadcom (AVGO) stock finished down 8% Friday, following a double-digit Thursday drop. Other AI-tied stocks were lower, including Arm Holdings (ARM), Marvell Technology (MRVL), Micron Technology (MU), Advanced Macro Devices (AMD), and Intel (INTC), which were all down between 11% and 17%. All of the Magnificent Seven tech giants were lower, with Nvidia (NVDA) and Tesla (TSLA) sinking more than 6% each.
Bitcoin fell below $60,000 for the first time since October 2024. Cryptocurrency-tied stocks Strategy (MSTR), Robinhood Markets (HOOD), MARA Holdings (MARA), and Coinbase Global (COIN) declined between roughly 6.5% and 11%.
The 10-year Treasury yield, which influences interest rates on mortgages and other consumer loans, was at 4.55% at 4 p.m. ET, up from 4.47% immediately before the jobs report, which indicated U.S. employers added 172,000 jobs in May, more than double the 80,000 consensus expectation of economists. The unemployment rate remained steady at 4.3%, as expected.
Per the CME FedWatch tool, investors now forecast that the Federal Reserve has about a 50% chance of raising interest rates at its late-October meeting, up from roughly 34% yesterday.
"It's easy to imagine potential shocks that could derail the job market's uptrend," Fifth Third Commercial Bank Chief U.S. Economist Bill Adams said in written commentary. "The Iran War and closure of the Strait of Hormuz are the big ones. They already caused real average hourly earnings to decline in the last two months. The longer the conflict drags on, the bigger its headwind will be for the cost of living, the job market, and the economy."
Oil prices declined further. West Texas Intermediate futures, the U.S. crude oil benchmark, pulled back 2.9% to $90.35 a barrel in recent trading, while front-month contracts of Brent crude, the global benchmark, settled down 2% to $93.09.
The U.S. dollar index, which tracks the value of the greenback against a basket of foreign currencies, was up 0.6% to 100.04. Gold futures fell 3.6% to $4,345 an ounce.
Lululemon Athletica (LULU) shares sank 8.5% after the athleisure retailer slashed its full-year revenue and profit projections, citing "headwinds."
JUNE 5, 2026 AT 08:11 PM GMT
Major Indexes Finish Lower for Week; S&P 500 Snaps 9-Week Winning Streak
The S&P 500 entered today on pace to end higher for a 10th straight week. It didn't come close.
The benchmark index saw its nine-week winning streak snapped with a 2.6% decline over the five sessions. It was its biggest weekly decline since May 2025.
The Nasdaq Composite finished down 4.7% over the five days, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average ended down 0.3%, with both failing to register a third consecutive week of gains. It was the Nasdaq's biggest weekly decline since April 2025.
For the year, the Nasdaq, S&P 500, and Dow are up roughly 11%, 8%, and 6%, respectively.
JUNE 5, 2026 AT 07:36 PM GMT
The SpaceX IPO Will Ripple Across Indexes and Funds. Here's What That Means—and Doesn't Mean
Major index providers, including the LSEG's FTSE Russell and the Nasdaq, have made it easier for new mega-cap stocks to land in their indexes. Those moves come ahead of expected offerings from SpaceX, as well as AI companies with massive private valuations, and they have some investors worried that the guardians of major market benchmarks were relaxing standards to stay relevant.
Space Exploration Technologies, or SpaceX, which could list next week under the symbol "SPCX," could gain fast-entry into some popular indexes, meaning buying from the funds that track those measures. Just not the S&P 500, which underpins the funds in which the great American investing public is most heavily invested.
S&P Dow Jones Indices, a subsidiary of S&P Global, on Thursday said it won't make the proposed changes to eligibility criteria that would have shortened the seasoning period required before companies can join the benchmark index and eased financial requirements to make room for new companies with huge market valuations. (That means SpaceX, but likely also companies like Anthropic and OpenAI.)
US Indexes Are Dropping After a Strong Jobs Report. Is the Labor Market a Problem for the Stock Market?
Businesses are hiring a little too much for Wall Street's liking.
The U.S. added 172,000 jobs in May, nearly twice what economists were expecting, while the unemployment rate held steady at a relatively low 4.3%. After stalling out last year, the job market has reaccelerated in 2026 despite the economic headwinds created by the war in Iran and the ongoing blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The number of job openings surged to a two-year high in April, according to data released earlier this week.
Stocks, however, sold off on Friday as investors shifted their interest-rate expectations for the remainder of the year. The S&P 500 was down more than 2% in recent trading, weighed down by a roughly 4% decline for tech stocks. It wasn't just the AI rally taking a breather Friday, however: Some two-thirds of the stocks on the New York Stock Exchange were recently in the red.
"Any hopes of a Fed rate cut have effectively been eliminated with this morning's strong jobs report," said Ronald Temple, chief market strategist at Lazard.
Intel Stock Took a Hit This Week After Its Record Rally. Here's How Much Traders See It Moving Next Week
Intel's stock took a big hit this week, bringing its record rally grinding to a halt. Could it signal more losses ahead, or leave the stock poised for a rebound?
The shares have fallen about 10% since the week began, making Intel (INTC) one of the biggest decliners in the S&P 500 this week, along with a number of other chip stocks amid some worries they may have climbed too high, too quickly. Even with its recent losses, Intel remains one the top gainers in the index for the year so far, up nearly 180% year-to-date and more than 400% over the last 12 months after a string of high-profile deals and signs of strong AI demand boosted optimism about a turnaround in its business.
Based on current options pricing, traders are now anticipating the stock could swing up to another 8% in either direction by the end of next week. A move of that size from Friday afternoon's level around $104 could see the shares rally back above $113, or slip as low as $96, giving up more of their gains this year.
The recent slide in Intel's stock has dragged it closer to Wall Street's consensus target around $95, per Visible Alpha data. Of the seven analysts with current ratings tracked by Visible Alpha, just three have said they consider the stock a "buy," compared to three neutral, and one sell rating.
Just 4 of 73 S&P 500 Information Technology Sector Components in Green Today
Today has been a particularly rough day for the S&P 500 Information Technology Sector.
Of the 73 stocks in the sector, just four are in positive territory Friday. It is down some 4.6%, by far the worst performances of the 11 sectors tracked by the benchmark index.
Tyler Technologies (TYL) is the biggest gainer of the bunch, up a mere 0.5%.
JUNE 5, 2026 AT 04:30 PM GMT
Bitcoin Falls Below $60,000 for 1st Time Since October 2024
Bitcoin—and cryptocurrency-tied stocks—are having a particularly rough Friday.
The world's largest cryptocurrency briefly fell below $60,000 for the first time since Oct. 11, 2024.
Crypto-tied stocks Strategy (MSTR), Robinhood Markets (HOOD), MARA Holdings (MARA), and Coinbase Global (COIN) dropped between 7% and 12% in recent trading.
"As global capital continues to flow toward AI and large-cap technology stocks, digital assets must compete with these high-growth sectors for investor allocation," Bitunix analyst Dean Chen wrote early Friday. "However, if investors eventually begin to question the sustainability of U.S. equity valuations, the pace of capital rotation and risk repricing could unfold far more rapidly than markets currently anticipate."
JUNE 5, 2026 AT 03:37 PM GMT
Lululemon Slashed Its Outlook. The Stock Is Plunging to Its Lowest Point Since 2018
A weaker outlook has Lululemon's stock plunging to its lowest level in years.
Shares of Lululemon Athletica (LULU) were down nearly 8% to $115 in recent trading, their lowest price since May of 2018, after the apparel maker lowered its full-year forecast. Lululemon said it now expects $11 billion to $11.15 billion in sales for the year, which would be flat to a 1% decline from last year, down from a previous forecast of $11.35 billion to $11.5 billion. Lululemon's second-quarter outlook of $2.45 billion to $2.48 billion in sales and earnings per share of $1.76 to $1.81 also came in well below what analysts were expecting, per Visible Alpha estimates.
Interim co-CEO Meghan Frank pointed to a drop in sales at the end of the first quarter and start of the second quarter amid "negative commentary in the media and on social channels," and said the company's recent product launches have had mixed performances, per an AlphaSense transcript.
JPMorgan analysts cut their price target for Lululemon's stock to $149 from $173 following the report, citing the weaker outlook and comments about Lululemon's recent product launches. The company posted earnings per share of $1.69 on $2.5 billion in sales in for the first quarter, roughly in line with analysts' estimates.
Cooper Paces S&P 500 After Stronger-Than-Expected Results
The Cooper Companies (COO) stock surged 8% to lead the S&P 500 Friday, a day after the medical devices maker's fiscal second-quarter results topped analysts' estimates.
Cooper posted adjusted earnings per share of $1.21 on revenue that increased 8% year-over-year to $1.08 billion. Analysts surveyed by Visible Alpha had expected $1.10 and $1.05 billion, respectively.
The San Ramon, Calif.-based firm kept its 2026 adjusted EPS forecast intact but lowered its organic revenue growth forecast to up 3.5% to 4.5%, down from the prior range of 4.5% to 5.5% growth, due to a reduction in its CooperVision (CVI) segment growth projection.
"Importantly, this softness is regional, not global, and we view it as temporary as Asia Pac resets amid economic pressure, especially in China and Japan, and to a lesser extent, Korea," CEO Al White said on the earnings call, per a transcript provided by AlphaSense. "Specifically, for CooperVision, we now expect Asia Pac to decline in Q3 with pressure from both the market and our ongoing rationalization of legacy hydrogel products."
Even including today's sharp gains, Cooper shares are down 18% this year.
JUNE 5, 2026 AT 01:55 PM GMT
The AI Boom Is Minting New Millionaires at the Fastest Pace in Years
The surge in AI stocks that's helped drive the market to record highs is also creating new millionaires at the fastest rate in years.
The world gained around 2 million new millionaires last year, marking the largest annual gain in five years, according to a recent report from French consulting firm Capgemini. The report found that stock market rallies across the globe, largely tied to the soaring value of AI companies, were the "primary engine" of their growing wealth.
In the U.S., the market's top tech stocks were responsible for about more than half of the benchmark S&P 500 index's 16.4% gain in 2025, according to research from Goldman Sachs.
By country, the U.S. minted the largest number of new millionaires last year at 736,000. That brought the number of millionaires in the country up to about 8.7 million people, or about 2.5% of the broader U.S. population.
Jobs Report Shows Hiring Shot Up in May as Labor Market Continues to Rebound
Forecasters were expecting the job market to extend its recent rebound. Instead, it shot up like a rocket.
U.S. employers added 172,000 jobs in May, while the unemployment rate remained at 4.3%, relatively low by historic standards, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said Friday.
The magnitude of job creation was more than double the 80,000 forecasters had anticipated according to a survey of economists by Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal. On top of that, April's job creation figures were increased to 179,000 from the 115,000 previously announced, while for March, the total was revised upwards to 214,000 from 185,000.
The solid hiring figures marked a distinct turnaround from last year and early 2026, when the market alternated between gaining and losing jobs each month and was pretty much treading water, as tariff-related uncertainty discouraged employers from expanding and bringing on new staff.
The job market has now added jobs for three months in a row, the first time that's happened since May 2025.
Gas Prices Have Dropped Every Day for 2 Weeks—See Where Drivers Are Paying the Most and Least
Drivers are finally getting a bit of relief at the pump after gas prices have declined for two weeks straight. Down 32 cents over that stretch, the national average for regular gasoline now stands at $4.24 a gallon, according to AAA.1
That's a notable improvement from the recent peak of $4.56 per gallon, which was first reached on May 7 and matched again on May 21. Prices have surged this spring due to the Iran conflict pushing oil prices sharply higher and rattling global energy markets.
Before the conflict began, drivers had been enjoying relatively low prices at the pump, with the national average holding in $2 territory for almost all of December, January, and February. It was the first sustained stretch in that range in almost five years.
That relative calm stands in contrast to how volatile gas prices can become during geopolitical shocks. For instance, the national average briefly topped $5 per gallon in June 2022 after Russia's invasion of Ukraine disrupted global oil supplies.
Could SpaceX Be Worth More Than Microsoft on Its IPO Day? Some Traders Are Betting on It
Could Elon Musk's rocket company rank among the Magnificent 7 on its debut day? Some traders are betting on it.
On prediction markets, some bettors figure that SpaceX's market capitalization will exceed $4 trillion by the end of its first day of trading, valuing the company more richly than Microsoft (MSFT) and possibly putting it in the neighborhood of Alphabet (GOOGL).
Clearly, there's euphoric sentiment around what is slated to be the largest IPO in history, seen landing next week: With SpaceX expected to have about 13 billion shares outstanding, not counting underwriters' options to purchase extra shares, a value of $4 trillion-plus would mean that shares would close above $300 apiece. That implies a first-day jump of 125%-plus from its expected IPO price of $135.
To be sure, the $4 trillion bet—which would put SpaceX somewhere in the top 5 of U.S. companies—is an outlier: The Polymarket event contract for it was recently priced at less than 2 cents, meaning the perceived odds of that happening, per bettors, are just 1%, down from 4% a couple of weeks ago.
